title: The Mental Game of Football - Brian Cain & Sean McDonnell
universal_lens: A finite attention budget is allocated across plays under irreducible uncertainty about which play is decisive; optimal policy is uniform vigilance, not retrospective weighting. The structural unification is a constrained minimax decision process on a discrete play index with unknown payoff-relevant subset, yielding one-play-at-a-time as the saddle-point policy under adversarial sampling of pivotal moments. Mental conditioning as a dynamical system with feedback loops between belief states, behavioral control, and performance outcomes.
gsi_mapping: GSI encodes each play as a conformal prediction instance where the nonconformity score is attentional drift from present-play processing. The one-play policy maintains valid coverage across a stream of plays; testimonial consensus functions as weakly labeled prior evidence that the system reduces emotional volatility, with Bayesian updating over coach/player reports rather than market prices. Bayesian belief updating framework for mental state transitions using prior probabilities of self-control and posterior evidence from play performance.
gse_mapping: GSE models game state transitions conditioned on present-play execution, not accumulated scoreboard emotion. The operator resets the state vector after each play and treats next-play transition probabilities as contextually independent given current situational variables, so emotional carryover is represented as a hidden state to be suppressed by a reset kernel. Conformal state-transition model mapping pre-play mental readiness to in-game decision-making and behavioral execution via cognitive load regulation.
